3. Set Focus mode to AF-S and AF-area mode to Single-point AF. Focus on a point about 2 m in front of the camera, then switch to MF so focus stays put.

5. Turn VR off while the camera is on the tripod. Use the 2 s self-timer or a remote release to reduce shutter-button shake.
6. Start around 1/60s as shown by the meter. Check the histogram and adjust exposure compensation if needed; protect bright sky highlights.
7. Review the foreground rocks and distant mountains at playback magnification. If the nearest rocks are closer than about 1 m, focus farther forward or use focus stacking.

why.reason: At 18mm, focusing around 2 m gives calculated sharpness from about 1 m to 94 m, covering foreground rocks through distant mountains.
The lowest native setting helps preserve image quality in a static landscape.
They reduce camera shake during the relatively slow golden-hour exposure.
It retains the warm golden-hour color while RAW files allow later white-balance adjustment.

pro_tips: Arrive early, compose the foreground rocks, and wait for a lull in the wind before taking the reflection frame.
